title: Viscous counterexample to locally self-similar blowup: the inner-profile exponent cannot exceed one half
author: Peter Constantin, Mihaela Ignatova, Vlad Vicol
work: On putative self-similarity for incompressible 3D Euler
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Proposition 3.1 (source label 'nse'), the viscous counterpart of the paper's self-similarity analysis: if a solution of the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equation splits into a regular part whose L^4(dt;L^2) norm is finite and an inner part supported in a ball of radius of order (1-t)^gamma whose L^2 norm is bounded by C(1-t)^{-1+3gamma/2}, then any blow up at time one forces gamma at most one half. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete argument that combines the two hypotheses rather than invoking a black box: it adds the inner and outer contributions to the L^4 norm of the vorticity, uses the explicit growth of the inner profile and the integrability of the outer part to bound the time integral by Gamma plus an explicit constant divided by 6 gamma minus 3, and then concludes that if gamma exceeds one half that integral is finite, which contradicts blow up by the classical regularity criterion. The bookkeeping of the exponent and the exact dependence on gamma is the point of the result, and it is research-level analysis of the Navier-Stokes equations rather than a qualifying-examination exercise.
